references.text: When Lot was led out of Sodom, he was told: 'Flee for your life!' — the same principle of fleeing a city under God's judgment without looking back ([ref:1 Mos 19:17|Genesis 19:17]).
Jeremiah urges Benjamin's children to flee from Jerusalem, for disaster threatens from the north — a prophetic call to leave Judea as judgment approaches ([ref:Jer 6:1|Jeremiah 6:1]).
Daniel describes those who escape and flee to the mountains, like doves in the valleys — an image of fleeing to the mountains in times of distress ([ref:Esek 7:16|Ezekiel 7:16]).

Matthew's parallel account of Jesus' speech, where he says that those in Judea must flee to the mountains and should not go down into their houses to get anything ([ref:Matt 24:16-18|Matthew 24:16-18]).
Mark's parallel text about the abomination of desolation, where those in Judea are urged to flee to the mountains ([ref:Mark 13:14|Mark 13:14]).
Jesus gives a similar warning: whoever is on the roof should not go down to get their belongings — the same theme of urgent flight without turning back ([ref:Luk 17:31|Luke 17:31]).

The Letter to the Hebrews describes people of faith who wandered in mountains and caves and holes in the ground — they fled to the mountains during persecution, just as Jesus urges here ([ref:Hebr 11:38|Hebrews 11:38]).
